name: AI asset discovery and posture (AI-SPM)
description: Finding every agent, MCP server, skill, model and tool in an organisation, including shadow AI, and ranking their risk

name: Agent runtime security (AI-DR)
description: Detecting and stopping risky agent behaviour while agents run: inline enforcement, guardrails, behavioural detection, kill switches

name: Agent identity and access control
description: Which identity an agent acts as, what it is allowed to access and do, least privilege and approval of agents

name: MCP and agent skills security
description: MCP servers, gateways, agent skills and tools: discovery, permissions, tool poisoning and attacks through MCP

name: AI red teaming
description: Testing agents and AI apps for weaknesses before attackers do: automated red teaming, multi-turn attacks, published attack research and vulnerabilities

name: AI supply chain security
description: Risk in models, open-weight weights, packages, repositories and tools that agents depend on

name: Coding and endpoint agents
description: Agents employees run on their machines: Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot and other coding assistants

name: SaaS and cloud agent platforms
description: Which agent platforms a competitor claims to secure: Microsoft Copilot Studio, Salesforce Agentforce, ServiceNow, ChatGPT and Claude Enterprise, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex

name: AI compliance and governance
description: Regulation and frameworks such as the EU AI Act, audit evidence, AI governance programmes

name: Category language
description: Terms competitors use to name the market and themselves, such as AI-SPM, AI-DR, agentic security, agent control plane, AI governance

name: Funding, M&A, partners and analysts
description: Funding rounds, acquisitions, partnerships, marketplace listings and analyst recognition such as Gartner or Forrester
